description: Bounded negative result for intent i014 (SNAPSHOT=s04, BRANCH=xsk-umem-rings). No credible double-fetch variant found in snapshots/s04 net/xdp. Evidence: (1) The seed's TX-metadata feature is entirely absent from s04 — grep for xsk_skb_metadata, XDP_TXMD, xsk_tx_metadata, tx_metadata_len, tx_sw_csum across net/xdp/, include/net/, and include/uapi/linux/if_xdp.h returns zero matches, so no csum_start/csum_offset/flags/launch_time UMEM-metadata reader exists to exhibit the pattern. (2) The ring-descriptor paths that do exist satisfy the single-fetch invariant: xskq_cons_read_desc (net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:199 '*desc = ring->desc[idx];') copies each user-mapped TX-ring descriptor once into a kernel-local struct xdp_desc before validation via xp_validate_desc (xsk_queue.h:133-189); xskq_cons_read_desc_batch (xsk_queue.h:224) copies into kernel-kvcalloc'd pool->tx_descs (xsk_buff_pool.c:47); __xsk_generic_xmit (xsk.c:536) uses a stack descriptor under xs->mutex; and all consuming sites (xsk.c:443-444, 489, 498, 509) read only the validated kernel-local copy, never the shared ring. Fill-queue readers (xsk_buff_pool.c:488/559; xsk_queue.h:115-121) likewise perform a single fetch into a local u64 with no check-then-use pair. Limitations: per-driver ndo_xsk_wakeup/ndo_xsk_xmit zero-copy implementations under drivers/net/ethernet/ were not line-by-line audited (they obtain descriptors only through the single-fetch helpers or kernel-resident tx_descs), and adjacent AF_XDP consumers outside net/xdp were only spot-checked. Full per-candidate evidence is in the final artifact at agent-state/findings/i014.json (snapshots_checked=["s04"], execution_status=complete, 5 candidates all classified safe, 0 findings).
